subject: Pricing sensitivity and burnpath — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing sensitivity and burnpath — post-demo next steps

Hi Kate — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can size a hosted pricing estimate that maps to your budget and procurement timeline.

Recap from the call:
- Primary workload: patient-facing conversational assistant + batch summarization of clinical notes (peak during business hours).
- Traffic shape: daytime spikes, predictable weekly cadence, occasional campaign-driven bursts.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in progress; procurement will need evidence (we can share SOC artefacts and an evidence pack).

What we need to confirm (quick replies appreciated):
1) Expected steady-state monthly token volume (ballpark). We discussed a rough band on the call — please confirm the number you expect to land in month 1 and month 6.
2) Peak TPS (tokens/sec or requests/sec) during your busiest windows — rough maximum concurrency to size burst capacity.
3) Target budget range for hosted inference (monthly run-rate). If you can share a $/month target or $/1M-token target, we will fit pricing bands to that.

Initial pricing context (for conversation only):
- Example unit-econ: $1,000 per 1M tokens (hosted) would translate to $X for your volume — we’ll run exact math once you confirm volumes.
- Key levers: batching, prefix caching, model variant (full vs quantized) — all of which materially change the $/1M outcome.

Attached is a first-pass pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx with three scenarios (conservative/likely/aggressive). I’ll put together a tighter estimate once you confirm items 1–3.

Next steps I propose:
- You reply with the quick numbers (1-3 above).
- We return a slimmed pricing sheet with per-slab $/1M and an explicit burst plan (canary + autoscale).
- If the numbers align, we prepare a mutual action plan and procurement checklist (SOC evidence + SOW).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if you prefer to talk through the numbers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Attachment: pricing_estimate_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 3 scenarios)
From: Kate Reynolds <kate@luminahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity and burnpath — post-demo next steps

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below so you can firm up the sheet: 

1) Monthly token volume: expecting ~42,000,000 tokens/month in steady state (month 1 might be nearer 30M while we ramp; month 6 we expect ~48M if adoption goes well).
2) Peak TPS: daytime peak concurrency hits about 220–260 TPS for short windows (10–20 minutes) — baseline business-hour TPS ~18–25. We also run a weekly batch at 0300 with a burst that is handled offline; not counted in TPS.
3) Budget range: procurement is looking for hosted solutions in the ~$40k–$60k/month window. We’d prefer to see a $/1M token equivalence so procurement can compare against other bids.

A few additional asks from procurement:
- A one-pager on fallback behavior during regional capacity constraints.
- Confirmation on whether prefix caching and batching are automatically enabled (we prefer those on by default unless there are API contract issues).

If you want to run numbers live tomorrow morning, I can free up 20 minutes.

—Kate
Director, Product Strategy
Lumina Health
Kate.Reynolds@luminahealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity and burnpath — post-demo next steps

Thanks Kate — this is perfect and very actionable. I ran the quick math from your numbers and sketched three hosted bands in the attached updated_pricing_estimate.xlsx; summary below: 

Quick math (illustrative):
- Baseline scenario: 30M tokens @ $1,200 / 1M = $36,000 / month
- Steady-state scenario: 42M tokens @ $1,000 / 1M = $42,000 / month
- High-adoption scenario: 48M tokens @ $925 / 1M = $44,400 / month (volume discount applied)

Notes and levers: 
- Peak TPS/burst: to comfortably handle 260 TPS short windows with low tail latency, we recommend reserving a small burst pool (predictable cost add-on) or enabling autoscale with a capped burst budget. I called this out as an optional line in the sheet.
- Caching & batching: prefix caching + continuous batching are enabled by default on our hosted API; we’ll mark whether any endpoints need cache bypass (e.g., for very low-latency single-shot calls). That improves unit-econ materially.
- Procurement asks: I’ve attached a one-page fallback summary and SOC evidence pointer in the Drive link; we’ll include a minimal MOP for regional fallback.

Requested next steps: 
- Confirm which pricing band you want us to model into a draft MSA/quote (Baseline / Steady-state / High-adoption). If you give a preferred band, we’ll produce a formal quote and a 12-month commitment option with a discount ladder.
- If procurement wants the $/1M broken down by model variant (full vs 8-bit quantized), tell me and marissa will include those columns.

I’ve attached updated_pricing_estimate.xlsx and included the HubSpot link for record DL-2039. If tomorrow AM works, I can do a 20-min run-through with procurement and marissa to lock the band.

Best,
Karthik

Attachment: updated_pricing_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with 3 bands + burst line-item)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/record/DL-2039
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing band recommendation for Lumina Health (DL-2039)

Looping internal commentary into the thread for Karthik’s inbox visibility (will not send external until we agree):

- Reviewed K’s quick math. Recommend we offer Lumina a 10% committed discount if they sign to a 12-month 48M tokens/mo commitment (effective unit price then ~ $832 / 1M). That keeps the band competitive with their target $40k–$60k/month while protecting margin.
- For the hosted quote, include a small burst allowance line (one-time activation + metered overage) and a clear description of autoscale limits.
- Add a procurement appendix that lists SOC artefacts and a short fallback MOP. Vanessa — can you draft the appendix and the short SLA bullet?

If K agrees, we can present the discounted 12-month option alongside the month-to-month steady-state band.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
